jobs.description:
Overview  

 
At QIAGEN, we are driven by a simple but powerful vision: making improvements in life possible.  

We’re dedicated to revolutionizing science and healthcare for the better. From our entrepreneurial roots to our current global presence, we've grown into a force for positive change. With thousands of employees across six continents, collaboration is our greatest strength. We’re always striving to identify talented individuals to join our exceptional teams. 
 
We have played a pivotal role in shaping modern science and healthcare, and we're just getting started. If you're someone who thrives on new challenges, values diversity and wants to make a tangible difference in people's lives, then QIAGEN is the place for you. 

 

At QIAGEN, every day is an opportunity to make a real-life impact. 

 

Join us, grow with us, and together, let's shape the future of biological discovery. 

‎

About this opportunity

In the position of a (Junior) Software Engineer (f/m/d) in Life Science and Diagnostics at QIAGEN, you will be making improvements in life possible – every working day. We are looking for you to help us shape our product development with skill and passion. You will work with our system and software teams to develop instrument control software for laboratory devices as well as data analysis software to process test results helping our customers to get valuable insights from a biological sample.

Your Tasks
* As a Software Engineer you will typically work in project teams of 5-10 people and gain experience in different roles throughout the life cycle of a software development project.
* You will start as a software developer or (automated) software tester in one of our scrum teams. Throught your professional career you will have the opportunity to grow into senior roles such as senior engineer, product owner, software architect or verification manager.  
* You will work across teams and across sites to generate the best possible solution for our products in a complex environment of Biology, Chemistry, Mechanics, Electronics and Software.
* You will be based at QIAGEN Hilden, our operational headquarter and will have the opportunity to visit our international development sites in Aarhus, Denmark or Wroclaw, Poland to strengthen and refine your software development capabilities.

Your Profile
* You have a master’s degree in computer science, with a minor in medicine, science or engineering
* You show a strong interest in software and product development and have already gained first professional experience.
* You love science and have a strong analytical mindset that strives to analyze, understand and solve problems.
* You are highly organized, work independently and easily adapt to changing work environment.
* You show excellent communication skills in both, English and German (C1 level)
* Ideally, you are familiar with working with AI-powered development tools or large language models to automate software development lifecycle processes. Experience with connecting AI agents with third-party systems using Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a plus

Please provide a transcript of record and an employer's reference if applicable.

What we offer  

 

* Bonus/Commission  

* Local benefits   

* Referral Program  

* Volunteer Day  

* Internal Academy (QIALearn)   

* Employee Assistance Program   

* Hybrid work (conditional to your role) 

 

Our people are the heartbeat of everything we do. Passion drives us as we push boundaries to innovate and evolve. We inspire with our leadership and make an impact with our actions. We cultivate a collaborative, supportive environment where each individual and team can flourish. We champion accountability and encourage entrepreneurial thinking.   

 

QIAGEN is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, status as a veteran, or disability.

The German Diabetes Center (DDZ), Leibniz Institute for Diabetes Research at Heinrich Heine University (HHU) Düsseldorf is an interdisciplinary research institute that integrates basic, translational and clinical research to improve the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of diabetes mellitus and its complications. The Institute for Clinical Biochemistry and Pathobiochemistry (Director: Prof. Dr. Hadi Al-Hasani) investigates the molecular mechanisms underlying insulin resistance, skeletal muscle metabolism and type 2 diabetes.

For a new research project, we are looking for a talented and highly motivated

Doctoral Student (PhD / Dr. rer. nat., m/f/div., E13 TV-L 65%)

to join our interdisciplinary research team investigating the molecular mechanisms by which repeated
cold exposure improves skeletal muscle insulin sensitivity.

Insulin resistance of skeletal muscle is a key feature in the development of type 2 diabetes, accounting for the majority of impaired postprandial glucose disposal. While lifestyle interventions such as exercise are well established, repeated cold exposure has recently emerged as a promising strategy to improve insulin sensitivity in humans, with reported improvements of up to 40%. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying these beneficial metabolic adaptations remain largely unknown.

The project aims to identify the signaling pathways responsible for cold-induced improvements in skeletal muscle insulin action. A particular focus will be placed on testing the hypothesis that mild cold-induced muscle activation ("micro-shivering"), rather than brown adipose tissue activation, mediates these metabolic benefits.

The project combines translational human studies with mechanistic investigations in mouse models and offers extensive training in state-of-the-art metabolic and molecular research techniques.
Proteomic analysis of human skeletal muscle biopsies obtained from cold acclimation studies to identify molecular signatures associated with improved insulin sensitivity.
Mechanistic studies in wild-type and UCP1-deficient mice to investigate the effects of cold exposure and muscle activation on glucose uptake and insulin action.
Functional characterization of established and novel regulators of skeletal muscle metabolism, including AMPK, GLUT4, Rac1 and newly identified candidate proteins.
Investigation of GLUT4 trafficking and insulin signaling using advanced molecular and cellular approaches.

The project offers training in:

Mass spectrometry-based proteomics
Mouse models of insulin resistance and metabolic disease
Indirect calorimetry and metabolic phenotyping
Glucose uptake assays in isolated skeletal muscle
Molecular biology techniques (Western blotting, qPCR, gene expression analyses)
Immunohistochemistry and skeletal muscle fibre typing

In vivo electroporation and functional gene manipulation
Fluorescence-based analysis of GLUT4 translocation

You hold (or are close to obtaining) a Master's degree in Biochemistry, Molecular Biology, Molecular Medicine, Physiology, Biomedical Sciences or a related discipline.
You have practical experience in molecular and cellular biology techniques such as Western blotting, qPCR and cell culture.
Experience with metabolic phenotyping, skeletal muscle biology, mouse models or proteomics is advantageous but not required.
You enjoy interdisciplinary research and are interested in combining human physiology with mechanistic laboratory studies.
You are highly motivated, curious, and able to work independently as well as collaboratively in an international research environment.
You have an excellent command of written and spoken English.

• Act as primary owner-side interface toward EPC contractors and key project consultants.
• Monitor contractor performance, schedule adherence, construction progress, and execution quality.
• Track contractual obligations, risks, variations, and claims in coordination with internal legal and management teams.

Technical & Advisor Coordination
• Coordinate external technical advisors, owner’s engineers, HSE consultants, commissioning specialists, and other technical stakeholders.
• Coordinate commissioning, performance testing, punch-list management, and COD activities.
• Support grid connection coordination together with external specialists and EPC contractors.

Construction & Site Coordination
• Coordinate site managers, HSE consultants, commissioning teams, and O&M stakeholders during execution.
• Conduct regular site visits during active construction and critical project phases.
• Monitor construction progress, interface management, quality issues, and project risks.

Commercial & Reporting Responsibilities
• Maintain project schedules, risk registers, action trackers, and reporting structures.
• Support budget monitoring and change-order tracking.
• Prepare project updates and reporting for senior management and internal stakeholders.

Operational Handover
• Coordinate project close-out, warranty management, defect resolution, and handover to asset management teams and investors.
• Support establishment of stable operational interfaces with O&M providers and operational stakeholders.

Your profileProfessional Experience
• Minimum 8 years of professional experience in utility-scale solar PV project delivery, thereof at least 3 years as main responsible project manager.
• Proven experience delivering at least 5 utility-scale PV projects to COD in Germany.
• Experience with PV+BESS hybrid projects is mandatory.
• Experience working on owner-side, EPC-side, or integrated developer/EPC delivery models.
• Exposure to EPCm, multi-contracting, or free-issue equipment models considered advantageous.
• Experience with MV grid connection projects required; HV/substation experience considered a plus.

Technical & Commercial Competencies
• Strong understanding of utility-scale PV construction and commissioning processes.
• Good understanding of project delivery interfaces including EPC contractors, technical advisors, grid operators, HSE, commissioning, and O&M stakeholders.
• Basic understanding of SCADA/PPC systems, EMS/BESS integration, protection systems and commissioning and performance testing.
• Familiarity with German grid connection processes, DSO coordination, and grid-code related execution topics considered advantageous.
• Experience with project schedule management, risk management, contractor coordination, and construction reporting.
• Familiarity with German permitting and environmental compliance processes.

Education & Background
• Degree or equivalent practical experience in engineering, renewable energy, construction management, project management, or related technical fields.

Language Requirements
• Fluent German and English required.
• German does not need to be native level but must be sufficient for interaction with contractors, authorities, DSOs, landowners, and project stakeholders.

Personal Profile
• Strong ownership mentality and proactive working style.
• Structured and solution-oriented approach to project execution.
• Comfortable operating in lean and fast-scaling organisations.
• Strong communication and stakeholder coordination capabilities.
• Able to work effectively under pressure and respond flexibly to changing project requirements.
• Cooperative but capable of assertive contractor management where required.
• High professional standards and strong commitment to project success and delivery quality.

Why us?
• Flexible working hours, work-from-home
• Exciting and responsible tasks with plenty of room for your own ideas
• Motivated team and flat hierarchies
• Internal and external training opportunities
• Permanent employment contract

About usAt Canopy Infrastructure, we're transforming the renewable energy landscape by developing utility-scale solar projects that create sustainable income streams for landowners while accelerating the clean energy transition.Our comprehensive approach combines technical expertise, financial innovation, and strategic partnerships to deliver projects that benefit communities, investors, and the environment.

jobs.occupation: Junior Innovation Project Manager (m/f/d) [temporary until February 2027] (Chemielaborant/in)
jobs.description:
Since our beginnings at Dr. Oetker, we have been breaking new ground. With pizza, cake, and desserts, as well as digital platforms and services - quality and an innovative spirit set us apart.

What awaits you? It's up to you! At Dr. Oetker, you can actively shape the future - both yours and ours. We want to be part of something bigger. Don't you?

JOIN THE TASTE.

YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

- As a Junior Innovation Project Manager (m/f/d), you will coordinate smaller renovation and innovation projects, overseeing them from the approved concept stage through to successful implementation. Your responsibilities will include ensuring that projects are completed on time while maintaining transparency regarding progress, risks and milestones.
- You will also support larger or more complex innovation projects, actively contributing to their implementation. You will also coordinate the market launch of existing sub-brands, product lines or products.
- You will coordinate cross-functionally and across countries to ensure feasibility and successful commercialization. Furthermore, you will oversee the briefing of R&D on formulation development and market research, as well as the finalization of technical specifications.
- Working closely with stakeholders, you will manage the project timeline and ensure timely implementation by all parties involved. As needed, you will coordinate project meetings and clarify actions and next steps.
- Using data, you will analyze volume estimates in collaboration with the markets. Together with relevant teams, you will identify dependencies and risks and develop mitigation plans.
- You will ensure that business cases are fully compiled and correctly entered into the Stage-Gate tool. You also enter relevant data into SAP and generate the necessary codes.

WHAT YOU BRING

- You have successfully completed a degree in business administration, Marketing, Innovation Management or a comparable qualification.
- You have experience in project management, particularly in innovation projects, and you are accustomed to working in teams and across functional boundaries.
- An international outlook and a strong entrepreneurial mindset shape the way you approach challenges.
- Strong assertiveness combined with excellent communication skills distinguishes you in daily interactions.
- You are willing to travel frequently. You are also motivated to collaborate with a diverse range of stakeholders.
- Excellent English skills complete your profile.

WHAT WE OFFER YOU

- Attractive remuneration
- Flexible work models & mobile work
- 30 days of vacation plus Special vacation at Christmas & New Year's Eve
- Onboarding and professional development opportunities
- Excellent employee restaurant and discounts in the Dr. Oetker Shop
- Events and celebrations ​
- Sports, health and fitness offers
- Pension plan, Sabbatical and JobRad
- Employee Assistance Program (EAP), this offers professional support in all situations, such as assistance with childcare, finding au pairs, and advice on care services.
- Daycare cooperation for children and laundry service

The Chair of Applied Geophysics at the Institute for Geosciences seeks the position of a

Doctoral Researcher in Seismology

Commencing at the earliest possible date.
We offer a part-time position (75%, 30 hours per week), limited to 3 years

Our research focuses on applied seismology, with an emphasis on induced seismicity, seismic monitoring, the absorption and scattering of seismic waves, and seismic noise. You will become part of a highly motivated team with a positive working atmosphere. You will support us in our research and make a significant contribution to the success of the applied geophysics team.
Determination of seismic attenuation in shallow subsurface layers using the spectral ratio method, utilising the ICDP Eger borehole seismometers
Calculation of earthquake source spectra, moment magnitude and spectral stress drop using the radiative transfer equation
Determination of frequency-dependent site amplification in the region’s station network
Carrying out 3-D attenuation tomography (t* tomography)
Processing and quality control of seismological data from the ELISE Large-N Experiment and permanent networks
Publication of results in international journals and presentation at conferences
Work on an own scientific qualification project, e.g. doctorate

University degree (Master’s degree) with a focus on geophysics, earth sciences with a specialisation in geophysics, physics or a comparable subject
Good knowledge of digital time-series signal processing
Sound knowledge of at least one programming language (Python, C, Fortran or equivalent)
Knowledge of wave propagation, seismic attenuation or tomography would be desirable
Good written and spoken English
We expect you to be a team player with strong interpersonal skills
Knowledge of German is an advantage, but not essential

An exciting field of employment and autonomous work at one of the largest employers in Thuringia.
You will work within national and international networks alongside renowned universities and research institutions
Participation in international conferences
A Graduate Academy for doctoral candidates and postdocs
Remuneration based on the provisions of the Collective Agreement for the Public Sector of the Federal States (TV-L) at salary scale E13 - depending on the candidate’s personal qualifications-, including a special annual payment in accordance with the collective agreement.
30 days of vacation per calendar year plus two days off on December 24 and 31

The advertised position is offered as a fixed-term position for 3 years.

Candidates with severe disabilities will be given preference in the case of equal qualifications and suitability.

Are you eager to work for us? Then apply by 26.09.2026 using our online form.

For further information on your application and the collection of personal data, please refer to our Privacy Statement for Applicants

We at Yara are part of a global network, collaborating to profitably and responsibly solve some of the world's key challenges - resource scarcity, food insecurity and environmental change.

About the Unit

Within Yara, Crop Nutrition and Biologicals Products R&D leads the development and innovation of our crop nutrition solutions. We generate scientific and agronomic insights through laboratory, greenhouse, and field trials; translate these into product concepts and development projects, and support the wider organization with robust, evidence-based knowledge.

We are seeking a curious, proactive, and impact-driven scientist to advance our product development and innovation pipeline for new fertilizers and sustainable technologies that complement and strengthen Yara’s premium crop nutrition portfolio. This role is an integral member of the Crop Nutrition and Biologicals Products R&D team and reports to the R&D Lead - Premium Products and Organics.

Scientist - Crop Nutrition Products (f/m/d)

Location: Dülmen, NW, DE
Area of Expertise: Research and Technology Product Development
Job Type: Permanent
Work mode (place): On-site + Home office
Job Requisition ID: 24724

Design and coordinate R&D projects focused on developing high-efficiency phosphorous (P) and nitrogen (N) fertilizer product candidates.
Plan, coordinate and execute internal and external research on agronomic efficiency, nutrient release, soil quality and the environmental impact of fertilizer product candidates.
Develop and implement methods to evaluate the mode of action and performance of new crop nutrition products.
Perform screening and proof-of-concept testing for products and technologies originating from scouting activities and third-party collaborations.
Represent Yara at scientific and technical events, industry associations, and forums related to new fertilizer technologies.
Collaborate with the Premium Products and Organics R&D Team and the broader Crop Nutrition and Biologicals Products R&D organization by contributing to additional projects as needed.

Master’s degree plus relevant applied research or industry experience in crop nutrition, soil science, fertilizers, or related fields. A PhD in agronomy, soil science, crop science, plant nutrition, plant physiology or a related discipline is a plus.
Deep understanding of N and P chemistry in soils, nutrient dynamics, and mechanisms of nutrient uptake, transport and assimilation in plants.
Strong scientific grounding in crop nutrition, soil processes, and agronomy, gained through academic research or professional R&D experience.
Knowledge of soil and fertilizer chemistry and plant physiological processes, with the ability to apply these concepts to product development.
Fundamental knowledge of fertilizer products (e.g., soil- and foliar-applied fertilizers, liquids, water-soluble fertilizers, fertigation products, coatings, and seed treatments) and application techniques/equipment.
Hands-on experience conducting laboratory, greenhouse, and/or field experiments, and proficiency in experimental design, analysis and interpretation of complex datasets.
Ability to translate scientific insights into practical recommendations for Yara’s premium crop nutrition products.
Collaborative mindset and ability to work in multidisciplinary and international teams.
Fluency in English; German is a plus.
The position is full-time, permanent, and based in Duelmen, Germany.

As a global organization we actively strive to reflect diversity in society. We therefore encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply. We are committed to creating a work environment that fits gender equality.

We Offer:

Permanent employment contract with industry-standard remuneration
Flexible working options
30 days' vacation entitlement
37.5 hours of basic working time with time recording (flexitime)

Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences
PhD Position (f/m/x) in Statistical Physics/Quantitative Biology

Institute for Biological Physics | research group of Professor Berg

We are one of the largest and oldest universities in Europe and one of the most important employers in our region. Our broad range of subjects, the dynamic development of our main research areas and our central location in Cologne make us attractive for students and researchers from around the world. We offer a wide range of career opportunities in science, technology, and administration.

The research environment at the University of Cologne provides an excellent setting for interdisciplinary doctoral training. PhD students have access to a broad range of
graduate-level courses and training opportunities through the graduate school BCGS (see https://www.gradschool.physics.uni-koeln.de/). The group is also embedded in a vibrant research landscape, especially the Collaborative Research Centre CRC1310 Predicting Evolution, which brings together researchers from different fields to model and forecast evolutionary dynamics (see https://crc1310.uni-koeln.de/).
We are looking for highly motivated individuals who enjoy working in an international team at the interface between statistical physics and quantitative biology.

The University of Cologne promotes equal opportunities and diversity. Women will be considered preferentially in accordance with the Equal Opportunities Act of North Rhine-Westphalia (Landesgleichstellungsgesetz - LGG NRW). We also expressly welcome applications from all suitable candidates regardless of their gender, nationality, ethnic and social origin, religion, disability, age, personal orientation and identity.

The position is available form 1 October 2026 on a part-time basis (19,92 hours per week). The initial appointment will be for three years, funds for an extension are available.If the applicant meets the relevant wage requirements and personal qualifications, the salary is based on remuneration group 13 TV-L of the pay scale for the German public sector.
Please apply online with proof of the required qualifications (a CV, publication list if applicable, and research statement, one letter of recommendation should be sent directly by the recommender to bergj@uni-koeln.de) without a photo.
The reference number is Wiss2608-15. The application deadline is 15 September 2026.
For further inquiries, please contact Professor Dr Johannes Berg (bergj@uni-koeln.de) and take a look at our FAQs. YOUR TASKS

Depending on the interests and background of the successful applicants, projects will be available in cancer evolution, resistance dynamics, and statistical modelling of the immune system. Projects involve concepts and methods from equilibrium and non-equilibrium physics and are often based on experimental collaborations.

For more details see www.thp.uni-koeln.de/~berg.

The position includes a standard teaching load (in English or in German) of 2 SWS alongside research activities.
YOUR PROFILE

Applicants should have a Master‘s in physics with excellent grades, a strong background in statistical physics, and a genuine interest in biology.
WE OFFER

Broad research and training opportunities within the graduate school BCGS
Close research group integration/supervision
A diverse working environment with equal opportunities
Support in balancing work and family life
Extensive advanced training opportunities
Occupational health management offers
Flexible working time models
Opportunity to work remotely

As the leading company in the field of software solutions for healthcare, we operate in 19 countries and employ over 9,000 dedicated staff members. You will work in a dynamic and innovative environment full of opportunities. With your commitment and passion, you have the chance to make a sustainable difference.

CGM Leverages AI: We’re looking for people who feel the power of AI in the e-health environment, who want to help shape change, and who are driven by a curious passion to see how technology can make healthcare smarter, simpler, and better.

Together, we are shaping the healthcare system of the future. Become part of our mission and make a difference - for a world where knowledge saves lives!

Are you passionate about groundbreaking products? Do you have the talent to turn ideas into real, valuable solutions-while always keeping the bigger picture in mind? Then we’d love to meet you!

You take end-to-end accountability for a large, distributed engineering organization that owns our ambulatory SaaS solutions and the shared framework modules used across all AIS DE products.

You co-define and drive the strategic product-technology roadmap for our cloud-based ambulatory portfolio in close collaboration with the executive leadership team.

You ensure that healthcare regulatory requirements-including medical device regulations, audits, and compliance-are rigorously embedded into product development, delivery, and operations.

You lead senior leaders and cross-functional teams, continuously increasing scalability, quality, AI maturity, and innovation velocity across products and platforms.

You represent the domain internally and externally, build strong executive-level stakeholder relationships, and position CGM as a leading SaaS provider in the Health-IT market.

Long-standing leadership experience at Director / VP / CTO level in SaaS product development, ideally with responsibility for large, distributed engineering organizations and complex product portfolios.

Exceptional academic background with a completed university degree and excellent grades, preferably in computer science, medical informatics, engineering, or a comparable technical field.

Deep expertise in cloud architectures and SaaS platforms, including modern DevOps practices and reliability engineering; hands-on experience with healthcare regulations (medical devices, audits, certifications) is a strong advantage.

Proven track record of driving AI adoption in engineering organizations, ideally with first-hand familiarity of Claude Code or comparable agentic coding tools (agents, skills, and workflows) and experience shaping AI pipelines, harnesses, and context engineering at organizational scale.

Excellent English and very good German, a strategic and entrepreneurial mindset, strong execution focus, outstanding leadership and communication skills, and the ability to guide complex organizations through transformation while staying clearly aligned with our healthcare purpose.

Mobile work: Work flexibly on the move two days a week and on site three days a week.

Attractive locations: In addition to fully equipped workplaces, regular events such as summer parties and Christmas parties await you at our locations.

Development: Our in-house academy and our portfolio of external cooperation partners will support you in your further development.

Health: Health is a valuable asset for us. Our in-house canteen offers a selection of tasty and healthy dishes every day, and we welcome you to our fully equipped fitness center for weekly courses (online & offline).

More is always possible: The kindergarten on our CGM campus in Koblenz helps our employees to organize their working day even more flexibly. We also offer corporate benefits, the option of a job bike, a company pension scheme, and much more.

Diversity is part of CGM! We look forward to receiving your application regardles...
